import re

def collapse_whitespace(s):
    result = re.sub(r'[ \t\r\n\x0b\x0c]+', ' ', s).strip(' \t\r\n\x0b\x0c')
    return result

def collapse_whitespace(s: str) -> str:
    """Collapse runs of ASCII whitespace into one space and strip ends.

    Preserves all non-ASCII whitespace characters (e.g. NBSP) and their order.
    """
    # Strip leading and trailing ASCII whitespace characters.
    s = s.strip(" \t\r\n\x0b\x0c")
    # Collapse any remaining run of those characters to a single space.
    import re
    return re.sub(r"[ \t\r\n\x0b\x0c]+", " ", s)
